# Shapes

<!-- generated by `python -m quality.sdk --reference`; edit the source, never this -->

`uv run python manage.py scaffold --list`, verbatim — every registered shape, its arguments, what it goes on and its golden. `on fresh-app`: an app `newapp` just made; `on noun`: a noun `scaffold noun` wrote, never a child row; `on app`: any product app; `on face`: the screen folder.

`event` writes the one `events.py` line, `<NOUN>_<PAST> = "<app>.<noun>.<past>"`, and nothing else; `verb` writes the service, that event, both doors and their tests, and after an `event` of the same verb it adopts the line `event` wrote (`adopted:`) instead of refusing it.

`verb <app> <Noun> <verb> --transition <from>-><to>` makes the verb one step of the noun's `scaffold enum`: its body is a `transition_<noun>` call from `<from>` to `<to>`, a press from any other value is `409 conflict`, and its test presses it once; without the flag a verb whose past tense names an enum value is inferred as that step.

`workflow <app> <Noun> <process>` (the approval wait) writes the run, its activities, its mark and its event, and the door that ends the wait: `approve_<noun>`, `POST /{id}/approve/` (`<noun>-approve`) and its MCP twin send the `approve` signal, and `<noun>.approve` is an administrator's at the row's own node (`may_archive`). Like every shape that writes policy lines, it then moves the noun's `<noun>_authz_baseline.json`: the noun's sweep re-run with the write asked, each key it added printed on a `baseline: … moved` line, so `feature.sh <app>` stays green.

A `child` or a `field` that names another app's noun: [A link between two apps](linking-apps.md) — no shape writes that foreign key.
